summary: Backend-only regression test of the Phase 55.12 bootstrap split (server.py -> bootstrap/{routers,lifespan,middleware}.py) and the removal of 4 dead revenue endpoints. Created /app/backend/tests/test_bootstrap_split_regression.py with 41 tests: health/boot, removed-endpoint 404s (HTTP + OpenAPI), retained revenue endpoint registration + auth gating, 9 critical endpoint smoke tests, middleware chain (gzip / CORS / security headers), and global exception handling. RESULT: 41/41 PASSED. Also did a cold `supervisorctl restart backend` and confirmed lifespan startup completes, /api/health returns 200 with import_failures=0, and no [IMPORT FAIL] lines in logs. No regressions found from the split.

minor.issue: FLAKY via public URL: returned a Cloudflare 502 HTML page once out of ~5 calls; 3 immediate retries and the in-process call (localhost:8001, 1.3s, 200) all succeeded. Appears to be preview-ingress flakiness, not app code. Test now retries once on 5xx. ~20% observed failure rate on first run.

Observability nit (pre-existing pattern, not caused by the split): none of the lifespan logger.info() lines ('Global httpx.AsyncClient created', 'BGE model + cluster cache preload kicked off', 'fast_search projection OK') appear in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. Root logger falls back to logging.lastResort (WARNING+ only, 'WARNING:root:' format), so logging.basicConfig(level=INFO) in server.py is not taking effect under uvicorn. The fast_search projection guard's ERROR branch would still surface, so impact is limited to boot diagnostics.

critical_code_review_comments: bootstrap/middleware.py:110-113 — global_exception_handler does `raise exc` for HTTPException from inside an @app.exception_handler(Exception). This works today only because Starlette's ExceptionMiddleware handles HTTPException before this handler is ever reached for normal routes; if an HTTPException is raised from inside a middleware it will escape as a raw 500 from uvicorn instead of JSON. Prefer `return await http_exception_handler(request, exc)`. (Pre-existing, carried over from old server.py — not a split regression.)

bootstrap/middleware.py:79-80 — `except RuntimeError: return JSONResponse(500)` in the security-headers middleware swallows ALL RuntimeErrors (not just 'No response returned'), bypassing the global exception handler and losing the system_errors log entry for those. Narrow the match on the exception message. (Pre-existing.)

bootstrap/routers.py:37-49 — the core-route batch import sets 15 routers to None on a single failure, so one broken core file silently degrades 15 surfaces and, unlike _safe_import, does NOT append to route_import_failures, so /api/health would still report import_failures=0. Recommend routing core imports through _safe_import too, or appending to route_import_failures in the except block.
seed_data_creation: None. All tests are read-only or auth-rejected; no revenue records or candidates were created.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New regression file: /app/backend/tests/test_bootstrap_split_regression.py (run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_bootstrap_split_regression.py -v, ~3 min). Two environment gotchas encoded in it: (1) /openapi.json is NOT reachable through the preview ingress (not under /api/*, returns the SPA) so route-registration assertions hit http://localhost:8001/openapi.json; (2) the preview ingress answers OPTIONS itself with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * before FastAPI sees it, so app-level CORS must also be asserted in-process. Also note two role-gate facts that look like failures but are by design: /api/notifications/history is require_role(['candidate']) (admin -> 403) and /api/employer/companies is require_role(['employer','recruiter']) (admin -> 403, recruiter -> 200).
rca_of_the_issue: No regression. The 4 initial test failures were all test-harness/environment artifacts, not product defects: 2 were admin hitting non-admin role gates (notifications/history is candidate-only, employer/companies is employer|recruiter-only — both returned 403 not 404, proving the routers registered fine after the split), 1 was the ingress overriding the CORS preflight with Allow-Origin '*' (app returns the correct https://ventureshrd.com in-process), and 1 was a transient ingress 502 on /api/analytics/admin. Middleware order is verified intact: gzip compresses /api/candidates?limit=50 (Content-Encoding: gzip), all 5 security headers plus the /api/* no-store Cache-Control are present, CORS echoes only allow-listed origins with credentials=true, and unhandled/unknown paths return JSON bodies (never HTML or a raw stack).
